# GpuFanController v1.7.1

Patch release fixing interactive installation and Nano-update prompts. Upgrade
the host package and download a fresh installer; Nano firmware remains **1.7.0**.
This supersedes v1.7.0 without modifying that immutable release.

## Fixes and improvements

- Fixed `File or stream is not seekable` when the installer or firmware updater
  opens its confirmation prompt. Both now use separate terminal input/output
  streams; confirmations are retained.
- Added explicit `--reinstall` to the firmware updater for supervised same-version
  flashing. It does not bypass identity, compatibility, EEPROM backup or
  post-flash checks. Already-current firmware is still skipped by default.
- Documented Bash's cached developer executable path (`hash -r` after migration),
  the old installer workaround, and the scope of the successful bench flash test.

## Compatibility

- Host: Ubuntu **24.04 amd64** with systemd; NVIDIA and experimental native-Linux
  AMD support are unchanged.
- Nano: classic ATmega328P, firmware **1.7.0**, protocol **2**, EEPROM schema **5**.
  There are no firmware source changes in this release.
- Existing host mappings, Nano configuration and calibration are retained.
  No Nano reflash or recalibration is required to obtain these installer fixes.
- `--yes` confirms host installation and skips the optional firmware question;
  it never authorizes a firmware write.

## Installation or upgrade

Download a new installer rather than reusing the broken v1.7.0 copy:

```sh
curl --fail --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
  https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/releases/download/v1.7.1/install.py \
  --output gpu-fan-install.py
# Inspect gpu-fan-install.py before running it.
python3 gpu-fan-install.py --version 1.7.1 --start
```

Run as your normal user; sudo is requested for package/service operations.
Firmware updates remain optional, separately confirmed and supervised. Stop GPU
workloads before interrupting cooling. See the
[installation and update guide](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.1/docs/RELEASES.md).

## Validation and limitations

- 25 release-policy tests passed locally, including real pseudo-terminal input,
  prompt output and EOF handling, optional-update consent, same-version reflash,
  wrong-identity/downgrade rejection, and EEPROM/flash failure safeguards.
- On September 10, 2026, the corrected updater reflashed the published 1.7.0 image
  onto an old-bootloader Nano under Ubuntu 24.04 WSL over USB/IP. Flash verified;
  complete before/after EEPROM reads were byte-identical, and controller identity,
  configuration, calibration and generations were unchanged. The release daemon
  restarted and resumed valid temperature forwarding from an internal Quadro P1000.
- This was a bench test with no GPUs dependent on the controller's fans. Supply
  and stopped-fan alerts remained visible. It does not establish cooling under
  load, first-time-board compatibility, universal clone-bootloader support or
  physical AMD validation. Existing hardware and safety limitations still apply.
- Publication is gated on the release workflow's host tests, firmware build and
  Ubuntu package install/reinstall/removal smoke test.

## Safety and support

This is a personal project provided as is, with no guarantees of compatibility,
cooling or reliability. Incorrect wiring/settings or failures can damage hardware
or cause data loss. Validate cooling on your system. Focused pull requests are
welcome, but a response, review or merge is not guaranteed; Issues and Discussions
remain disabled.

See the [risk notice](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.1/README.md#use-at-your-own-risk),
[MIT license](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.1/LICENSE) and
[support policy](https://github.com/MikeInNs/GpuFanController/blob/v1.7.1/SUPPORT.md).
